author.name: Susan Sontag
author.heading: About Susan Sontag
author.bio: Susan Sontag wrote essays and fiction that joined close attention to art with arguments about public life. Against Interpretation questioned habits of criticism, On Photography examined images, and Illness as Metaphor challenged moral meanings imposed on disease.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The opening imagines health and illness as territories into which everyone may have to travel. Sontag then examines how diseases acquire punitive and romantic meanings, arguing against treating illness as evidence of a patient’s moral character.
